modelIntro.title: What Makes Wan 3.0 a Major Video Generation Upgrade?
description: Wan 3.0 moves the Wan family beyond isolated short clips toward complete, production-ready sequences. Native 4K output preserves product labels, faces, fabric, architecture, and fine lighting detail, while a 30-second generation window gives a scene enough time for an opening, development, and closing image without stitching several unrelated clips together.

The larger change is continuity. Wan 3.0 can organize up to six connected shots while keeping the same character, product, location, lighting direction, and visual language across cuts. Add up to 12 reference images for identity, wardrobe, product design, environment, and style, then generate picture and synchronized sound together. The result is better suited to advertising, character-led storytelling, cinematic previsualization, and branded content than a single impressive but disconnected shot.

metrics.label: Native 4K output
metrics.value: Generate at up to 3840 × 2160 for sharper faces, packaging, textures, typography, wide establishing shots, and commercial masters that need room for reframing.

metrics.label: Up to 30 seconds
metrics.value: Fit an opening hook, product or character development, and a closing beat inside one generation instead of matching several short clips in post-production.

metrics.label: Six connected shots
metrics.value: Plan wide shots, close-ups, tracking moves, reaction shots, inserts, and a final composition while preserving one coherent scene.

metrics.label: Character consistency
metrics.value: Maintain facial identity, wardrobe, body details, and signature styling across camera angles and separate videos for recurring characters and campaign series.

metrics.label: Up to 12 reference images
metrics.value: Assign references to the character, product, location, costume, color palette, lighting, and visual style without forcing one image to communicate every constraint.

metrics.label: Synchronized audio
metrics.value: Generate ambience, material sounds, action cues, dialogue timing, and music direction with the picture so sound follows what happens on screen.

metrics.label: Cinematic camera control
metrics.value: Describe push-ins, pull-backs, pans, orbit moves, crane shots, follow shots, lens distance, and shot scale as part of a structured sequence.

howToUse.title: How to Create a Wan 3.0 Video

steps.title: Choose text or image as the starting point
steps.desc: Start with text-to-video when the full scene can be described from scratch. Use image-to-video when a character, product, location, or opening composition must match a visual reference.

steps.title: Build a focused reference set
steps.desc: Use separate images for identity, wardrobe, product design, environment, lighting, and style. Remove references that introduce conflicting faces, colors, camera angles, or art direction.

steps.title: Write the sequence shot by shot
steps.desc: Give every shot a subject, action, framing, camera move, and transition. Then list the details that must remain unchanged across all six shots.

steps.title: Set output and generate
steps.desc: Choose aspect ratio, duration, resolution, and audio settings for the destination. Review continuity first, then refine individual motion, timing, or sound cues in the next generation.

promptExamples.title: Wan 3.0 Prompt Examples
promptExamples.subtitle: Each prompt demonstrates a different Wan 3.0 strength: connected shots, identity continuity, multi-reference control, or synchronized sound.

items.title: Six-Shot Luxury Watch Commercial
items.prompt: Create a connected luxury watch commercial. Shot 1: wide symmetrical view of a dark museum display. Shot 2: slow push-in as a narrow light moves across the steel case. Shot 3: macro view of the engraved crown turning. Shot 4: the same watch appears on a tailored wrist beside a city window. Shot 5: orbit around the dial as reflections shift from blue to gold. Shot 6: centered product close-up with the logo fully readable. Keep the watch proportions, dial layout, metal finish, and brand typography identical. Match each cut with restrained mechanical clicks and quiet gallery ambience.
items.description: Uses six connected shots to test product accuracy, lighting continuity, camera coverage, readable branding, and synchronized material sound.

items.title: Recurring Character Night Story
items.prompt: Use the character references for the same woman, yellow raincoat, short dark hair, and silver earrings. Shot 1: she waits inside a glass bus shelter in heavy rain. Shot 2: close-up as reflected headlights move across her face. Shot 3: side tracking shot when she leaves the shelter. Shot 4: wide view as she crosses the empty road. Shot 5: follow shot toward a warm apartment entrance. Shot 6: close-up as she looks back before the door closes. Preserve her face, wardrobe, height, and color palette in every shot. Add rain on glass, distant buses, footsteps, and a final door latch.
items.description: Tests a recurring character across changing shot scales, reflections, locations, motion, and environmental audio.

items.title: Twelve-Reference Design Hotel Film
items.prompt: Use the supplied references for the hotel exterior, lobby geometry, guest character, uniform, brass signage, furniture, suite, rooftop pool, food styling, sunset palette, lens treatment, and brand typography. Build a connected arrival story from the exterior to check-in, elevator, suite reveal, rooftop dinner, and final skyline logo frame. Keep architecture, guest identity, materials, signage, and warm editorial color consistent. Use slow crane, tracking, and orbit movements with lobby ambience, elevator chime, water, cutlery, and distant city sound.
items.description: Assigns a distinct role to a large reference set while preserving architecture, guest identity, brand details, and one visual language.

items.title: Sound-Synchronized Ceramic Process
items.prompt: Follow one ceramic artist making a cup in a quiet studio. Begin with clay landing on the wheel, move to hands centering it, show the walls rising in close side view, cut to the rim being trimmed, reveal the finished glaze, and end with tea pouring into the same cup. Keep the artist hands, clay color, tools, wheel, table, and studio light unchanged. Synchronize the clay impact, wheel vibration, wet hand contact, trimming scrape, kiln door, ceramic tap, and final pour with the exact actions.
items.description: Builds the edit around physical sound cues and tests hand-object interaction, material continuity, and precise timing.

troubleshooting.title: Prompt Tips for Better Wan 3.0 Results
troubleshooting.subtitle: Treat the prompt as a compact production brief. Define the sequence, continuity rules, camera language, and audio timing before adding style words.

items.title: Write one clear line for every shot
items.desc: Weak prompt: Make a cinematic product video with different angles. Better prompt:
items.prompt: Shot 1: wide tabletop reveal. Shot 2: macro view of the material. Shot 3: side tracking shot during use. Shot 4: close-up of the logo. Keep product shape, color, label placement, light direction, and background consistent across every cut.

items.title: Separate fixed details from changing action
items.desc: Weak prompt: Keep the character consistent while she moves through the city. Better prompt:
items.prompt: Keep the same face, hairstyle, red coat, black boots, and gold necklace in all shots. Only the camera angle, walking direction, background location, and weather reflections may change.

items.title: Give each reference one responsibility
items.desc: Weak prompt: Use all references to make the video look right. Better prompt:
items.prompt: Use image 1 for facial identity, image 2 for wardrobe, images 3 and 4 for product geometry, image 5 for the room layout, image 6 for color palette, and image 7 for lens and lighting style. Do not blend clothing or architecture between references.

items.title: Attach sound to visible events
items.desc: Weak prompt: Add realistic synchronized audio. Better prompt:
items.prompt: Match a soft metal click when the clasp closes, two footsteps as the subject crosses frame, a short elevator chime when the doors open, and lower city ambience during the final close-up.

faq.a: Wan 3.0 is Alibaba’s next-generation AI video model for native 4K text-to-video and image-to-video creation. It expands the Wan family with longer 30-second clips, connected multi-shot generation, stronger consistency, more references, cinematic camera direction, and synchronized audio.

faq.q: What makes Wan 3.0 different from Wan 2.7?
faq.a: Wan 3.0 increases output from 1080p to native 4K, extends the generation window from 15 to 30 seconds, supports up to six connected shots and 12 reference images, and places more emphasis on character continuity across shots and videos.
Yes. Wan 3.0 targets native 4K output up to 3840 × 2160, preserving more detail for faces, products, materials, typography, cropping, and commercial delivery.
Yes. Wan 3.0 can generate clips up to 30 seconds, enough for an opening, several connected story or product beats, and a closing composition in one sequence.

faq.q: How many shots can Wan 3.0 generate?
faq.a: Wan 3.0 can organize up to six connected shots in one generation. Write each shot separately and state which character, product, location, lighting, and style details must remain consistent.

faq.q: How many reference images can I use?
faq.a: Wan 3.0 supports up to 12 reference images. Use them for separate responsibilities such as character identity, wardrobe, product design, environment, props, color palette, and visual style.
Yes. Wan 3.0 generates audio with the video, including ambience, action sounds, dialogue timing, music direction, and transitions that follow visible events.

faq.q: Can Wan 3.0 keep the same character across videos?
faq.a: Character consistency is a central Wan 3.0 strength. A focused identity and wardrobe reference set helps preserve the same face, styling, and proportions across shots, locations, and related videos.

faq.q: Is Wan 3.0 good for product advertising?
faq.a: Wan 3.0 is well suited to product films because native 4K preserves labels and material details, multi-reference input controls product and brand assets, and connected shots can cover reveal, detail, use, and closing frames.

faq.q: Wan 3.0 or Seedance 2.0: which should I choose?
faq.a: Choose Wan 3.0 for long native-4K sequences, character or product continuity, and large image-reference sets. Choose Seedance 2.0 when multimodal reference video, reference audio, and director-style scene planning are more important.

faq.q: Wan 3.0 or Kling 3.0: which is better for motion?
faq.a: Choose Kling 3.0 for high-energy action and aggressive camera movement. Choose Wan 3.0 when the larger challenge is keeping a cast, product, location, and sound coherent across a longer multi-shot sequence.

faq.q: Wan 3.0 or Veo 3.1: which should I use?
faq.a: Choose Veo 3.1 for photorealistic individual shots, dialogue, and cinematic atmosphere. Choose Wan 3.0 for connected shot coverage, larger image-reference sets, recurring characters, and a full 30-second sequence.
